newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST -- U.S. Nov PPI seen rising modestly.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST -- U.S. Nov PPI seen rising modestly.

text.p: U.S. wholesale prices remained under control in November and are likely to trigger only a modest increase in the Producer Price Index for the month, analysts said.
The numbers will be released by the Labor Department at 0830 EST/1330 GMT on Wednesday, December 11.

"There's not much that will be notable about these numbers. Energy prices are trending higher, food prices are trending downwards, and overall there seems to be little inflation in the pipeline," said David Jones, chief economist at Aubrey G. Lanston & Co Inc.
Jones expects overall PPI as well as core PPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, to rise 0.2 percent in November.
According to a Reuters survey, U.S. economists on average expect overall PPI for November to rise only 0.3 percent compared to a 0.4 percent rise in October.

But they expect core PPI to rise 0.2 percent, compared to a drop of 0.3 percent in October. Most economists believe core PPI in November is likely to be higher than last month because October's figures included prices on new car models, which tend to be volatile.

"Last October was only the second time in the last 30 years that new car model prices were lower than they had been compared to the previous year. The only other time it happened, prices bounced back half a percent in November," said Mark Lasky, senior economist at DRI/McGraw Hill, who expects core PPI to rise by 0.3 percent in November.
"November's number will still be moderate from a long-term perspective, but it will also show that core PPI is not as benign as we might have thought last month," he added.
The energy component of PPI, which has been on the rise in recent months, is expected to moderate in November.

"Basically given that prices are in the $25 a barrel range, it's difficult to see further upside (to PPI). Most of the rise from $18 to $25 from earlier months is already factored in," said Ram Bhagavatula, chief financial economist at Citicorp Global Finance.
There is less consensus about food prices, however.

Bhagavatula and Aubry G. Lanston's Jones said food price increases should ease in November becuase an unexpectedly strong growing season has lowered U.S. prices on basic crops such as wheat, corn and soybean.

"We have already seen prices fall if you look at wheat and corn futures. We're likely to see that translate to finished goods," says Bhagavatula. Both economists expect only a 0.2 percent increase in overall PPI.
But Lasky expects food prices to come in stronger than last month. "Even though grain prices were down, people don't consume grains directly, so they don't affect finished good prices," he said.
Lasky said spot prices of poultry and eggs were up strongly in November, which should push up PPI to 0.3 percent.
He noted that food prices are an important component of PPI, making up 23 percent of the overall number.
